newsitem.title: RUSSIA: OLYMPICS-CHERNOMYRDIN TELLS IOC RUSSIA MUST GET GAMES.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-CHERNOMYRDIN TELLS IOC RUSSIA MUST GET GAMES.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin kept up heavy political pressure in support of St Petersburg's bid for the 2004 Olympics on Monday, telling the International Olympic Committee Russia must get the Games.

"In Russia there is a firm conviction that St. Petersburg can and should become the capital of the Olympic Games," Interfax news agency quoted Chernomyrdin as telling IOC president Juan Antonio Samaranch in a telephone call.
The IOC will announce the five final candidates from the current 11 contenders on Friday and will make its final choice on September 5.

Chernomyrdin, who has headed St. Petersburg's bid but will be absent from the final meetings in Lausanne this week because of political commitments in Moscow, urged Samaranch to listen to Russia's complaints about the IOC's evaluation of the city.

Russian officials protest that the IOC conclusion that staging the Games would cost the decaying former tsarist capital nearly $10 billion failed to take account of a government pledge to spend more than $7 billion on infrastructure and sports facilities for the city's tercentenary in 2003, Olympics or not.
Moscow says winning the Games would be an international stamp of approval for its moves to democracy.
Rome and Athens are among the front-runners for the event.
